title: Turmeric Black Pepper Gargle

seo.title: Turmeric and Black Pepper Gargle for Sore Throat and Cough
seo.description: A warm turmeric gargle with a pinch of black pepper and salt, traditionally used to ease throat irritation in respiratory cough and congestion.

purpose: A warm gargle traditionally used to soothe a scratchy throat and support comfort in cough with congestion.
dosage: 1 cup for gargling; do not swallow unless a practitioner advises
anupana: Not swallowed; spit after gargling, then sip warm water if the mouth feels dry
traditional_context: Haridra (turmeric) with a pinch of Maricha and warm saline water is a common kitchen practice for Galashosha and Kasa. The gargle is local, heating and kapha-reducing, intended to comfort the throat rather than treat deeper chest disease.

ingredients_list.notes: Optional if the throat is already burning

preparation.step: Warm 1 cup of water until it is hot but comfortable to hold in the mouth. Do not use boiling water.
Stir in 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, a pinch of rock salt, and an optional pinch of black pepper.
Gargle for 20-30 seconds and spit. Repeat until the cup is finished.
Rinse the mouth with plain warm water to limit turmeric staining.

precautions.precaution: The liquid should be warm, never scalding. Test the temperature before gargling.
Do not use this gargle on an open mouth ulcer if it stings badly; stop if pain increases.
Turmeric stains fabric and sinks. Use a cup you do not mind colouring.

who_should_avoid.warning: Young children who cannot gargle and spit safely should not use this remedy.
People with turmeric or pepper allergy, or a severely inflamed throat, should seek clinical advice instead.
